Let's outline final:

Title: "Short answer"
- Eid al-Fitr is not a public holiday in Canton Aargau/Switzerland. No automatic right to a paid day off solely because it's Eid.
- But as an employer, you must not treat her unfairly/discriminatorily. If Thursday is truly impossible to staff, you can require her to work or require vacation/unpaid. If you can cover with reasonable effort, granting or accommodating is the safer/fairer option.

"Legal background (Aarau/Switzerland)"
- Public holidays: cantonal; Eid not included.
- Vacation: OR 329a: employer sets timing, can refuse for operational reasons, but must not be arbitrary/discriminatory.
- Unpaid leave: no right; by agreement.
- Non-discrimination/good faith: OR 327b/327c, constitutional equality; religious belief protected; refusal solely due to religion problematic. Operational necessity can justify.

"Fair test"
1. Check contract/policy/past practice.
2. Clarify what she needs: full/half day, time for prayer, exact date.
3. Assess operational impact: can you cover Thursday? staffing, appointments, safety, cost.
4. Look for least restrictive alternative.
5. Decide and document.

"Options for Thursday"
- If you can cover: grant as paid religious leave (goodwill) or as vacation if she has entitlement.
- If you cannot cover full day but can cover half: half-day off, staggered shift, leave morning for Eid prayer.
- If full day not possible: ask her to use vacation if available; if not, unpaid leave; or swap with willing colleague; or work Thursday and take a different day if religion allows (probably not for Eid but for family celebration maybe).
- If no arrangement: require attendance; explain operational reasons.

"Sample responses"
- If accommodating: "I can approve Thursday morning as vacation/unpaid..." etc.
- If refusing full day: "I understand... Thursday is fully booked... I can't give an unplanned paid day. Options: use vacation if you have enough, unpaid leave, half-day, swap. Please confirm by X."
- If she has no vacation and you won't allow unpaid: "We need you on shift; if you cannot work for religious reasons, we must discuss, but the shift remains scheduled." (cautious)

"Consistency and documentation"
- Apply same criteria to all; don't target religion; document business reasons, alternatives considered, communications.
- Avoid saying "we don't give Islamic holidays." Say date conflicts with staffing.
- If you grant as paid, consider general policy to avoid favoritism.

"Long-term policy"
- Create religious leave policy: e.g., major religious holidays may be requested as vacation/unpaid; up to X days; subject to operational approval; 2-week notice; manager will try to accommodate.
- Cross-train staff, leave calendar.

"Red flags"
- Don't force proof; don't retaliate; don't make colleague feel forced; don't unilaterally dock pay without agreement; don't treat as sick leave.

"When to get advice"
- If she threatens complaint, if you have policy, if you want to pay, if you are unsure. Contact Aargau labor inspectorate, employer association, Swiss labor lawyer.
